entries.name: Asupersync
entries.text: dicklesworthstone asupersync asupersync framework an experimental rust async runtime that uses region-owned tasks, explicit cancellation protocols, capability-gated effects, and deterministic replay testing. experimental rust systems that can validate selected adapters and cancellation boundaries teams investigating structured shutdown and reproducible concurrency failures systems-and-infrastructure libraries testing observability security build-backend-services test-software rust region-owned tasks that close to quiescence instead of detaching children request, drain, and finalize cancellation protocol for covered primitives capability-gated runtime-managed effects and obligation tracking lab runtime with virtual time, deterministic scheduling, and trace replay tokio compatibility layer and native runtime, synchronization, and channel primitives rust crate command-line binary webassembly browser packages cargo git dependency build from source rust javascript typescript rust edition 2024 webassembly tokio compatibility layer licenseref-mit-openai-anthropic-rider mit license with openai/anthropic rider makes task ownership and cancellation boundaries explicit in the runtime model includes deterministic scheduling and replay facilities for concurrency testing documents compatibility and platform boundaries in detail production cleanup budgets are advisory; non-cooperative work can continue past its budget and public i/o entry points do not all check capabilities the project describes itself as experimental and pre-1.0, not an established broad runtime replacement default contributor and release lanes require a pinned nightly rust toolchain; a restricted stable subset is documented it is not drop-in compatible with tokio-bound crates, and some adapters and platform paths remain scoped or partial the nonstandard license rider materially limits who may use or receive the software async runtime for rust where correctness is structural: region-owned tasks, cancel-correct protocols, capability-gated effects, and deterministic replay testing async concurrency runtime rust structured-concurrency

the documentation cites costs in the thousands or tens of thousands of dollars scans need provider credentials such as a direct openai or anthropic api key or vercel ai gateway; vercel-hosted worker sandboxes require a vercel account the retained evidence establishes no github project release deepsec is a security harness for finding vulnerabilities in your codebase powered by coding agents
